Referral Note

22-year-old college senior referred by Student Health Services for evaluation of worsening anxiety in social situations. He reports intense fear whenever he is expected to speak in class, give presentations, eat in public, meet unfamiliar people, or participate in group discussions, and worries that others will judge him negatively, think he is unintelligent, or notice that he appears anxious. Because of these fears he has declined leadership opportunities, stopped attending several classes that require presentations, and avoids social gatherings whenever possible, although he wants close friendships. Symptoms began during high school and have progressively worsened throughout college. He denies panic attacks outside social situations, obsessive thoughts, hallucinations, mania, substance use, and suicidal or homicidal ideation. Physical examination and routine laboratory studies at Student Health are unremarkable. Referred for psychiatric evaluation.

Behavioral Observations (on arrival)

Appearance: Appropriately groomed.

Behavior: Cooperative. Eye contact is limited.

Speech: Soft but coherent.

Mood / Affect: Describes mood as “nervous”; affect restricted but appropriate.

Thought / Perception: Thought processes logical and organized. Thought content negative for psychosis, suicidal ideation, or homicidal ideation.

Cognition / Insight: Alert and fully oriented. Insight and judgment intact.
